title: Starting & Running a Small Business
subtitle: Turn an idea into a business: research the market, plan, fund, launch and grow it.
outcomes: Explain what entrepreneurs do and the traits that help them succeed
Research a market and write a business plan
Estimate startup costs, choose a legal form and find funding
Manage, market and grow a small business

lessons.title: Ready, Set, Start Your Own Business
Using AI in a small business
Trends in Entrepreneurship and Small-Business Ownership

toc.text: Into the Future: Start-ups Drive the Economy
How Far Will You Go to Get Rich?

pool.q: Into which categories do entrepreneurs fall, according to the lesson?
pool.explain: Each type approaches new ventures differently.
pool.evidence: Types of Entrepreneurs Entrepreneurs fall into several categories: classic entrepreneurs, multipreneurs, and intrapreneurs.

pool.q: Who are classic entrepreneurs?
options: Employees who never leave a large company
Risk-takers who start their own companies based on innovative ideas
pool.explain: Some are micropreneurs who plan to stay small.
pool.evidence: Classic Entrepreneurs Classic entrepreneurs are risk-takers who start their own companies based on innovative ideas.

pool.q: How do entrepreneurs differ from typical small-business owners?
options: They are less likely to accept the status quo and take a longer-term view
They focus only on this month's sales
pool.explain: Entrepreneurs look for change and long-term opportunity.
pool.evidence: Entrepreneurs are less likely to accept the status quo, and they generally take a longer-term view than the small-business owner.

pool.q: Besides managerial and technical ability, what does being an entrepreneur require?
options: Drive, perseverance, passion and a spirit of adventure
pool.explain: Successful entrepreneurs also share other characteristics.
pool.evidence: Being an entrepreneur requires special drive, perseverance, passion, and a spirit of adventure, in addition to managerial and technical ability.

pool.q: What kind of risk do most successful entrepreneurs prefer?
options: A moderate degree of risk where they can better control the outcome
pool.explain: They avoid ventures where luck plays a large role.
pool.evidence: Risk-takers: Although they are not averse to risk, most successful entrepreneurs favor business opportunities that carry a moderate degree of risk where they can better control the outcome over highly risky ventures where luck plays a large role.

pool.q: What does being self-confident mean for an entrepreneur?
options: Understanding the challenges and being decisive and confident in solving problems
pool.explain: Confidence comes with understanding the challenges.
pool.evidence: Self-confident: They understand the challenges of starting and operating a business and are decisive and confident in their ability to solve problems.

pool.q: Why do some mid-career employees leave the corporate world for small business?
options: Because small firms always pay more
In search of the new opportunities that self-employment provides
Because corporations have no jobs at all
pool.explain: Independence and a better lifestyle attract them.
pool.evidence: Mid-career employees leave the corporate world—either voluntarily or as a result of downsizing—in search of the new opportunities that self-employment provides.

pool.q: What does market research help you do?
pool.explain: Competitive analysis then helps make the business unique.
pool.evidence: Market research helps you find customers for your business.

pool.q: What does competitive analysis help you do?
pool.explain: Combine both to find a competitive advantage.
pool.evidence: Competitive analysis helps you make your business unique.

pool.q: When can market research reduce risks?
options: Only after ten years of trading
Only after you close the business
Even while your business is still just an idea
pool.explain: It confirms and improves your business idea.
pool.evidence: Market research lets you reduce risks even while your business is still just a gleam in your eye.

pool.q: How does the SBA describe the business plan?
options: An optional document for big companies
pool.explain: It guides each stage of starting and managing the business.
pool.evidence: Your business plan is the foundation of your business.

pool.q: What can a business plan help you get?
pool.explain: Investors and partners read the plan.
pool.evidence: Business plans can help you get funding or bring on new business partners.

pool.q: How will you use your business plan?
options: As a roadmap for how to structure, run and grow your business
Only once, then throw it away
pool.explain: A good plan guides you through each stage.
pool.evidence: You’ll use your business plan as a roadmap for how to structure, run, and grow your new business.

pool.q: What is the first step in starting your own business?
options: Borrowing as much money as possible
A self-assessment of whether you have the traits to succeed and which business suits you
pool.explain: Then you find the idea and plan.
pool.evidence: Getting Started The first step in starting your own business is a self-assessment to determine whether you have the personal traits you need to succeed and, if so, what type of business would be best for you.

pool.q: What share of business start-ups involve brand-new organisations?
pool.explain: The rest are purchased companies or franchises.
pool.evidence: About 75 percent of business start-ups involve brand-new organizations, with the remaining 25 percent representing purchased companies or franchises.

pool.q: What is the break-even point?
options: Where total cost equals total revenue, with no loss or gain
When the loan is fully repaid
pool.explain: It is important in any plan shown to investors.
pool.evidence: The break-even point is the point at which total cost and total revenue are equal, meaning there is no loss or gain for your small business.

pool.q: Why calculate your startup costs?
options: To request funding, attract investors and estimate when you'll turn a profit
Because it is the only legal requirement
pool.explain: Understanding expenses helps you launch successfully.
pool.evidence: Calculate the startup costs for your small business so you can request funding, attract investors, and estimate when you’ll turn a profit.

pool.q: What is self-funding (bootstrapping)?
options: Using your own financial resources to support your business
pool.explain: It can include savings or family and friends.
pool.evidence: Loans Self-funding Investors Otherwise known as bootstrapping, self-funding lets you leverage your own financial resources to support your business.

pool.q: What is the trade-off of self-funding?
options: You lose control but share the risk
You pay high interest to a bank
You keep complete control but take on all the risk yourself
You must give investors seats on the board
pool.explain: Control and risk go together.
pool.evidence: With self-funding, you retain complete control over the business, but you also take on all the risk yourself.

pool.q: In what form can investors fund a start-up?
pool.explain: Investors provide capital in exchange for a stake.
pool.evidence: Investors can give you funding to start your business in the form of venture capital investments.

pool.q: What is a sole proprietorship?
options: A business established, owned, operated and often financed by one person
A business owned by the government
pool.explain: It is the easiest form to set up.
pool.evidence: a business that is established, owned, operated, and often financed by one person

pool.q: What is a major disadvantage of a sole proprietorship?
options: It has too many legal requirements
It must have a board of directors
pool.explain: Lenders view it as high risk.
pool.evidence: Disadvantages of Sole Proprietorships Along with the freedom to operate the business as they wish, sole proprietors face several disadvantages: Unlimited liability.

pool.q: Why is a written partnership agreement recommended?
options: Because partnerships are illegal without one in all countries
To prevent later conflicts between the partners
pool.explain: It records purpose and each partner's contributions.
pool.evidence: A written partnership agreement, spelling out the terms and conditions of the partnership, is recommended to prevent later conflicts between the partners.

pool.q: Whom do nearly all small businesses need, according to the lesson?
pool.explain: A CPA helps with record keeping, decisions and tax planning.
pool.evidence: Nearly all small businesses need a good certified public accountant (CPA) who can help with financial record keeping, decision-making, and tax planning.

pool.q: How does the owner's role change as the company grows?
options: Others make many day-to-day decisions while the owner manages people and plans long term
The owner does every task alone
pool.explain: A larger firm may also need more managerial talent.
pool.evidence: As the company grows, others will make many of the day-to-day decisions while the owner focuses on managing employees and planning for the firm’s long-term success.

pool.q: What is one way to ease the burden of managing a business?
pool.explain: Consultants can be used as needed.
pool.evidence: Using Outside Consultants One way to ease the burden of managing a business is to hire outside consultants.

pool.q: What is the foundation of managing your finances, according to the SBA?
pool.explain: It tracks capital and supports cash flow projections.
pool.evidence: The balance sheet is the foundation of managing your finances.

pool.q: Why categorise expenses in your balance sheet?
options: To hide costs from the tax office
To separate costs such as development, operations, recurring and nonrecurring costs
To make the balance sheet longer
pool.explain: Categorised expenses help you manage finances.
pool.evidence: From development and operations to recurring and nonrecurring costs, it’s important to categorize expenses in your balance sheet.

pool.q: How can AI help a small business, according to the SBA?
options: It can help the business do more with less
It replaces the need for customers
pool.explain: Read about both the risks and the benefits.
pool.evidence: As a small business owner, AI can help your small businesses do more with less.

pool.q: What can AI do with your small business data?
options: Analyse it and pick out common themes
pool.explain: Use your own client data for better decisions.
pool.evidence: AI can help you analyze your small business data and pick out common themes.

pool.q: Where does much entrepreneurial opportunity come from?
options: Major changes in demographics, society and technology
pool.explain: At present all three are changing together.
pool.evidence: Much entrepreneurial opportunity comes from major changes in demographics, society, and technology, and at present there is a confluence of all three.

pool.q: Between 2007 and 2017, how fast did women-owned firms grow compared with all businesses?
pool.explain: Women-owned firms had the highest growth rate.
pool.evidence: Between 2007 and 2017, women-owned firms increased by 114 percent, compared to a 44 percent increase among all businesses.
